briefing.headline: The simulation predicts that leaving more than doubles: about 1,305 departures in the next 12 months versus 573 under today's hybrid model, roughly 730 extra exits (+126%), taking annual attrition from about 11% to 26% of the workforce.
briefing.most_at_risk: Managers (+177%), caregivers (+162%) and people with long commutes (+151%) react worst, because three extra days of 1–1.5 hour commutes collide with young children, elderly parents and late US calls, and competitors still offer the hybrid work they would be giving up.
risks: Losing managers and team leads at the highest rate (+177%) puts client delivery and team stability at risk; they are the hardest to replace and may take their teams with them.

Tying attendance to performance ratings removes any quiet flexibility and lands hardest on caregivers, so the policy is likely to be seen as unfair and could damage your appeal to parents and people caring for elderly relatives.

Even employees with short commutes and no caring duties say they will 'quietly look around'. Exits may come gradually over the year as competitor offers arrive, so early attrition figures could look fine and give false reassurance.
design_changes: Remove attendance from performance ratings. Voices repeatedly name it as the factor that turns annoyance into job-hunting.
Move to three set office days rather than five, or phase toward more days with a review point. A smaller step keeps you closer to competitors' hybrid offers.

Add explicit flexibility for late client calls, such as working from home or starting later on days with evening US or Europe calls, plus defined provisions for caregivers and very long commutes; voices say a shuttle alone won't fix an 85–98 minute commute.
briefing.confidence: low, the direction is consistent across every group, so a sharp rise in leaving is credible, but the exact numbers rest on only 48 modelled voices (about two per group), and most voices describe 'quietly looking' rather than resigning, so how many actually leave is the most uncertain part; treat 1,305 as a warning signal, not a forecast.
